articles.body: A major settlement involving a Texas land developer has brought renewed attention to complaints about how residential plots were marketed and financed in communities outside Houston. Colony Ridge Land LLC and its affiliates have agreed to pay $68 million to resolve lawsuits brought by federal authorities and the State of Texas over alleged deceptive sales practices and lending arrangements. The agreement also addresses concerns about flooding in the developments, with $18 million earmarked for drainage improvements. Other parts of the deal cover housing affordability, loan defaults, foreclosure prevention and law enforcement. The company will also face restrictions on selling newly developed residential plots directly to consumers.How Colony Ridge came under federal and state scrutinyColony Ridge operates as both a land developer and a lender in the Houston area. Its business involved selling residential lots to buyers, with financing offered through loans arranged by the company itself. This model became the subject of legal scrutiny after concerns emerged over the way properties were advertised and the terms on which buyers were encouraged to purchase them.The US Department of Justice's Civil Rights Division and the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau filed a lawsuit against the company in December 2023. The State of Texas brought a separate case in March 2024 through its Office of the Attorney General. Both cases raised allegations concerning the sale of land and the financing offered to purchasers.Federal investigators alleged that Hispanic consumers were deliberately targeted through advertisements and sales approaches that did not always give an accurate picture of the properties. The investigation also raised questions about whether prospective buyers were properly informed about flooding risks and the actual condition of the lots being offered.According to the Justice Department, the lending arrangements allowed buyers to take out seller-financed loans without a proper assessment of whether they could afford the repayments. Authorities argued that this exposed borrowers to a greater risk of falling behind on payments, with foreclosures adding to the financial difficulties faced by some households.$18 million allocated to tackle flooding problemsOf the $68 million settlement, $48 million will go towards infrastructure across the Colony Ridge developments. Drainage work accounts for $18 million of that amount, while the remaining $30 million is intended for other infrastructure improvements.Flooding had featured among the complaints surrounding the properties. The federal investigation specifically pointed to alleged misrepresentations about flood risks during the sales process. The drainage allocation is intended to address damage to homes caused by severe flooding and improve infrastructure in the affected residential areas.The distinction between the two infrastructure allocations is important. The $18 million is specifically designated for drainage, while the additional $30 million covers broader improvements. The settlement does not describe the entire $48 million as flood-control funding.New lending rules and measures to reduce foreclosuresThe agreement also changes how Colony Ridge can assess buyers seeking financing for residential lots. The developer will have to introduce underwriting standards that take account of a borrower's income, assets and existing debts before approving a loan.This requirement addresses one of the central concerns raised in the lawsuits: that loans were being issued without sufficient checks on whether purchasers could manage the repayments. Under the new arrangement, the company must consider a buyer's financial circumstances rather than rely on the previous lending approach described in the investigation.There are separate obligations concerning borrowers who have already fallen behind on payments. Colony Ridge must establish a plan to help customers avoid default and work towards reducing the overall default rate. It will also have to introduce a policy aimed at reducing the number and frequency of foreclosures and deeds in lieu of foreclosure.Credit reporting is another part of the settlement. The company must develop a plan to address damage to borrowers' credit arising from reports it made in connection with defaulted lot loans. This provision covers borrowers who have defaulted on loans issued by Colony Ridge.Changes to property advertisements and buyer disclosuresThe settlement places new requirements on how the developer describes the land it sells. Advertisements will have to provide accurate information about the properties and the loan terms attached to purchases. The agreement is intended to prevent buyers from being given an inaccurate impression of what they are paying for.Pre-sale disclosures will also have to clarify the actual condition of a property. In particular, the company must accurately state whether a lot or property is ready for someone to move into and whether it has access to all city services.$20 million for law enforcement and a three-year development restrictionBeyond housing and lending, the agreement includes $20 million for increased law enforcement presence in the Colony Ridge communities. The money is intended to support public safety and help the developments comply with existing local, state and federal agreements.The settlement also places a significant restriction on the company's future development activity. Colony Ridge must halt the development of new residential plats intended for direct-to-consumer sales for three years. This limits its ability to continue that particular model of residential land sales during the period covered by the agreement.There are also provisions concerning the documents buyers must present when purchasing land. The settlement refers to an intrastate land sales exemption under the Interstate Land Sales Full Disclosure Act (ILSA). Purchasers will be required to provide specified identification, including an unexpired Texas driver's licence or state identification card, certain qualifying limited-term Texas licences, or an eligible passport accompanied by a valid visa.What the $68 million agreement means for the lawsuitsThe settlement brings together two rounds of legal action, one filed by federal authorities in December 2023 and another brought by Texas in March 2024. The Justice Department said the agreement followed coordinated work between its Civil Rights Division and the Texas Attorney General's Office.The financial commitment is spread across several areas rather than being limited to compensation or infrastructure spending. It includes drainage and other improvements, tighter lending assessments, measures addressing defaults and foreclosures, changes to property advertising, and additional law enforcement funding.Disclaimer: This article is based on publicly available information released by the US Department of Justice. The allegations described in the lawsuits and the terms of the settlement have been reported as stated by the authorities. The Times of India has not independently verified the claims.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Kevin Durant bought an Arizona mansion from NFL star DeAndre Hopkins for nearly $13 million in 2023; three years and a move to Houston later, the 1.72-acre home has returned to the market for $13.9 million
articles.summary: Kevin Durant has relisted his Paradise Valley, Arizona mansion for $13.9 million, three years after buying it from NFL star DeAndre Hopkins for $12.9
articles.body: Kevin Durant has relisted his Paradise Valley, Arizona mansion for $13.9 million, three years after buying it from NFL star DeAndre Hopkins for $12.9 million. The Houston Rockets player first tried to sell the home in September 2025 at $14.495 million, then cut the price before pulling it from the market, according to Realtor.com and Sports Illustrated.The 1.72 acre property is now back on the market as Durant settles into his next chapter in Houston. The home, which served as his primary residence during his time with the Phoenix Suns, is being listed by Alexa Kort of The Beverly Hills Estates along with Adam Bowman and Brian North of Compass. Read more details about it, as per the reports, here:How the home changed handsDurant bought the Paradise Valley mansion in 2023 from DeAndre Hopkins for $12.9 million. The purchase came shortly after Durant was traded from the Brooklyn Nets to the Phoenix Suns. The home was used as Durant’s primary residence during his two and a half year run with the Suns. After he was traded to Houston in 2025, the property became less central to his life.Durant first tried to sell the home in September 2025 for $14.495 million. He later reduced the price to $13.995 million before taking it off the market entirely.What the mansion includesThe home was designed by architect Jack DeBartolo and spans 10,865 square feet. It sits on a 1.72 acre lot and includes five bedrooms and eight bathrooms. Inside, the property features poured in place concrete walls, gallery like corridors, floor to ceiling glass, and custom finishes. The living room includes a fireplace, while the kitchen has a black marble island and high end appliances. The primary suite opens directly to the outdoor area. The bathroom includes a marble bath and dual vanities, and the home also has a movie theater, sauna, steam shower, and custom closet space, as per the reports by Realtor and Sports Illustrated.What makes the outdoor space stand outOne of the biggest draws of the property is its 2,000 square foot garage, which is designed to showcase a large vehicle collection. The garage is large enough to hold several cars and is a key feature for buyers interested in luxury vehicles.Outside, the home includes an 82 foot lap and reflecting pool. The property also offers panoramic views of Camelback Mountain, the Praying Monk, and Piestewa Peak.The outdoor space is designed to blend with the desert landscape. The views and the pool area give the home a resort like feel while maintaining privacy.Why Durant is sellingDurant’s move to Houston is a major reason the home is back on the market. He was traded from the Suns to the Rockets in July 2025 and has remained with Houston since then.The trade was part of a historic seven team deal that sent Jalen Green and Dillon Brooks to Phoenix along with multiple draft assets. Durant later signed a contract extension with the Rockets in October 2025.With his career now centered in Houston, the Arizona mansion is no longer part of his day to day life. That has made selling the property a practical next step.What happens nextThe home is now listed at $13.9 million, slightly below its original asking price. Whether that price will attract a buyer remains to be seen, but the property’s design and location give it a strong appeal.For Durant, the sale marks another step in moving on from his time in Phoenix. For the next owner, the home offers a mix of privacy, luxury, and views that are hard to find in the Paradise Valley area.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? Build Your Legacy with TOI Homes.

articles.title: In 2006, the Sherman family bought a Miami island property for $17 million and built an 18,213-square-foot waterfront mansion; the estate, with 320 feet of bay frontage, is now listed for $170 million
articles.summary: A Miami Beach estate on La Gorce Island has been listed for $170 million, making it one of the most expensive homes ever offered in the city.
articles.body: A Miami Beach estate on La Gorce Island has been listed for $170 million, making it one of the most expensive homes ever offered in the city. The property was bought by the Sherman family for $17 million in 2006 and later developed into an 18,213 square foot waterfront mansion, according to Realtor.com, Robb Report, and The Real Deal.The estate sits on a 1.23 acre point lot at the tip of the guard gated island, with 320 feet of Biscayne Bay frontage. Built in 2015, the home is now being sold by Betsy Sherman, the widow of former Campbell’s Company chairman George Sherman, who died in 2021.How the estate came togetherThe Shermans purchased the land in 2006 for $17 million. Over the next several years, they built a custom home that was completed in 2015. The result is a two story contemporary main residence and a detached guesthouse. Together, they offer eight bedrooms, 12 full bathrooms, and four powder rooms.The property is now listed at $170 million, a price that works out to roughly $9,330 per square foot, as per the reports. If it sells near that figure, it would rank among Miami’s most expensive residential sales ever.What the home includesThe main house features a skylit entry foyer with a sculptural spiral staircase. From there, the great room opens to a covered terrace through walls of sliding glass. The home includes a formal dining room that seats up to 14, a den, and a kitchen centered on a large eat in island. Upstairs, the primary suite has its own sitting area, balcony, and dual baths.Other spaces include an executive office, a dedicated screening room, and a fitness studio with a yoga nook overlooking a bamboo garden. The guesthouse has its own kitchen and living area, while the garage can hold up to four vehicles.Why the waterfront mattersThe estate’s biggest asset is its location. It sits on a point lot with 320 feet of open Biscayne Bay frontage, offering water views from nearly every room. Outside, the grounds feature a swimming pool, raised spa, alfresco kitchen, and dining pavilion. The property also includes a deep water dock designed to accommodate large yachts.The setting is part of La Gorce Island, a tightly held enclave that has attracted residents including Matt Damon, Ricky Martin, Billy Joel, and Cher. The island’s privacy and waterfront access make it one of Miami’s most desirable addresses.Why the owners are sellingBetsy Sherman told The Wall Street Journal that she is reluctantly parting with the home. She said it feels like the right time for another family to enjoy the property. She plans to move back to Fisher Island, where she and George previously owned a condo purchased from Oprah Winfrey. The move reflects a shift in how she wants to live going forward.The listing is held by Jill Hertzberg and her children, Danny and Hillary Hertzberg, of the Jills Zeder Group at Coldwell Banker. Hertzberg described the estate as one of the crown jewels of Miami.What the sale could meanThe $170 million asking price puts the estate in rare company. It matches the record set earlier this year by Mark Zuckerberg and Priscilla Chan on nearby Indian Creek Island.The home’s combination of size, privacy, and waterfront frontage makes it a standout in the Miami market. Whether it reaches its full asking price remains to be seen, but the listing has already drawn attention.For now, the estate is on the market as one of Miami’s most ambitious listings. Its history, design, and location make it a property that goes beyond a typical luxury home.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? Build Your Legacy with TOI Homes.

articles.title: More than 65,000 Americans who sent money through Walmart stores are now receiving refunds after scammers took millions from customers; FTC is distributing over $9.8 million
articles.summary: More than 65,000 Americans are receiving refunds after losing money to scammers who used Walmart stores to collect payments through the retailer’s wire
articles.body: More than 65,000 Americans are receiving refunds after losing money to scammers who used Walmart stores to collect payments through the retailer’s wire transfer services. The Federal Trade Commission (FTC) has announced that it is distributing more than $9.8 million to consumers affected by the alleged failures in Walmart’s fraud prevention measures. The payments follow a settlement reached in 2025, after the agency accused the retailer of allowing fraudsters to exploit its money transfer services and take hundreds of millions of dollars from customers.Walmart scam refunds reach more than 65,000 affected consumersAccording to the FTC’s October 15, 2026, press release, the agency is sending cheques to 65,022 consumers whose money transfers were connected to the case. The total amount being distributed exceeds $9.8 million, providing financial relief to people who were affected by fraudulent transactions carried out through Walmart’s money transfer services.The refunds are intended for customers who completed eligible money transfers at Walmart between January 2015 and December 2024. The FTC confirmed these dates on its official Walmart refunds information page, explaining who qualifies for the payments.The agency is distributing the money directly through cheques rather than requiring affected customers to submit new refund applications. This means eligible recipients do not need to pay a fee to receive their money.The payments are part of a wider consumer protection action against Walmart, following allegations that the retailer did not take sufficient steps to prevent scammers from using its services.How did scammers use Walmart stores to take customers' moneyThe FTC's case centred on fraudsters who persuaded consumers to send money through Walmart's wire transfer facilities. These services allowed customers to transfer funds through participating Walmart locations, but the agency alleged that the system was repeatedly exploited by scammers.According to the FTC's lawsuit, Walmart failed to properly secure its money transfer services, train employees to recognise suspicious transactions and warn customers about the risks of fraud. These shortcomings allegedly made it easier for criminals to collect money from people who believed they were making legitimate payments.What did the FTC lawsuit reveal about the retailer's safeguardsThe original complaint, filed in June 2022 in the US District Court for the Northern District of Illinois, described several weaknesses in Walmart's money transfer operations.The FTC alleged employees were not trained to spot suspicious transactions or to question customers who might be sending money to fraudsters. It also highlighted concerns about identity checks, inadequate warnings about fraud and failure to stop suspicious payments being collected.The complaint lays out the many ways the scammers took advantage of these vulnerabilities. They included plots to pose as government agents, lottery and prise scams and so-called grandparent scams where criminals pretended to be relatives in urgent need of financial help.Older Americans and others who were already financially struggling were affected. The agency also said the fraudsters could collect the payments in cash from various Walmart stores, making it harder for victims and law enforcement officials to trace the recipients.The 2025 settlement led to a $10 million judgmentThe case settled in June 2025, when Walmart agreed to pay a monetary judgement of $10 million. The agreement is described in the FTC case records as a stipulated order for an injunction and monetary judgement.Under the order, Walmart must take timely and appropriate measures to detect and prevent fraudulent money transfers. It is also prohibited from knowingly processing or paying out transfers that result from fraud.However, the settlement did not mean that Walmart admitted the allegations. The stipulated order specifically states that the company neither admitted nor denied the complaint's allegations. The FTC's case summary confirms that the settlement resolved the charges brought against the retailer and led to the consumer compensation programme.How can recipients claim their Walmart scam refundsThe FTC has advised eligible consumers who receive a refund cheque to cash it within 90 days. The deadline is also printed on the cheque, so recipients should check the payment document rather than leave it unattended.According to its October 2026 announcement, the FTC's enforcement actions resulted in more than $435 million in consumer refunds during 2025.You use AI every day. articles.title: BJP launches push to add eligible voters in city
articles.summary: BJP held workshops across Lucknow’s six assembly segments under Matdata Jodo Abhiyan to boost voter enrolment, corrections and outreach to eligible voters.
articles.body: Lucknow: BJP on Thursday organised workshops across all six assembly segments of Lucknow metropolitan area as part of its ‘Matdata Jodo Abhiyan’ (voter enrolment campaign), aimed at accelerating voter registration and ensuring that eligible citizens are included in the electoral rolls.The workshops brought together party office-bearers, assembly in-charges, booth-level workers and campaign volunteers, who were urged to actively identify eligible but unenrolled voters, facilitate corrections in voter lists and assist citizens in getting their names added to the rolls.Separate workshops were held in West, North, East, Central, Cantonment and Sarojininagar assembly seats, attended by senior BJP MLAs and party functionaries. Deputy chief minister Brajesh Pathak participated in the Cantonment assembly workshop, while BJP Lucknow Metropolitan president Anand Dwivedi attended key sessions.Pathak stressed that an accurate and updated voter list was essential for “strengthening” democracy. He called upon workers to conduct door-to-door outreach, encourage citizens to verify their names on the electoral rolls and help eligible voters complete the registration process.BJP state vice-president Neeraj Singh described the campaign as a significant democratic exercise and urged workers to reach first-time voters, youth and those whose names are missing from voter lists.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Lucknow | Silver Rate in Lucknow | Bank Holidays in Lucknow | Public Holidays in Lucknow | Lucknow AQI | Weather in Lucknow | Petrol Price in Lucknow | Diesel Price in Lucknow | CNG Price in Lucknow | LPG Price in LucknowStay updated with the latest Lucknow news. articles.title: Tarique Rahman's aide alleges forged Hasina signature in fresh letter seeking passport, NID
articles.summary: DHAKA: Bangladesh has questioned the authenticity of a fresh letter reportedly sent by London-based Matrix Chambers to the Acting High Commissioner of
articles.body: DHAKA: Bangladesh has questioned the authenticity of a fresh letter reportedly sent by London-based Matrix Chambers to the Acting High Commissioner of Bangladesh in New Delhi concerning former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina's passport and National Identity Card (NID).Prime Minister Tarique Rahman's political aide Md Rashed Khan alleged that Hasina's signature had been forged in the letter sent to the Bangladesh High Commission in New Delhi.Bangladesh has repeatedly sought Hasina’s extradition, but India has declined to hand her over. She first announced in August her intention to return to Bangladesh in December.In a Facebook post, Rashed claimed that officials at the Bangladesh High Commission had examined the letter and found evidence of signature forgery."I spoke in detail with an official working at the Bangladesh High Commission in New Delhi. After verification, they found that the signature on the letter had been forged," he said.Rashed questioned how a different signature could be used in an application involving Hasina, arguing that an individual's signature should remain consistent with the one previously used and recognised in official documents, particularly the NID.He claimed that Hasina had used her signature in Bengali in all official documents during her tenure as Prime Minister, and that any application of this nature should not carry a different or forged signature."Sheikh Hasina is one individual, and she should have only one signature," Rashed said, adding that a signature different from the one recorded in her NID could not legitimately be used in such an application.He also questioned why the lawyers at Matrix Chambers had not checked the language of Hasina's signature before sending the letter."Thieves always leave some clues behind. Matrix Chambers has made the same mistake while allegedly forging Sheikh Hasina's signature in the letter," he said.Rashed further remarked that the lawyers could have checked with Hasina whether she signed in Bengali or English before submitting the correspondence.The documents in question were also shared by Awami League leaders through their verified social media accounts.However, the authenticity of the letter and the allegation of forgery could not be independently verified.In a letter emailed to the Bangladesh High Commission in New Delhi earlier this month, Hasina’s counsel urged the top diplomat to take necessary action to provide her with a passport and national identity card.The letter, sent by London-based law firm Matrix Chambers, asked the mission for the application to be processed “expeditiously” on the basis of Hasina’s Bangladeshi nationality and in accordance with “obligations arising under international human rights instruments.”Hasina fled to India after student-led protests had forced her from power on August 5, 2024 and had since then remained there.In 2025, a Bangladeshi special tribunal sentenced her to death for crimes against humanity committed during the mass uprising, ruling that she had been responsible for ordering the crackdown, which left hundreds of people dead and thousands of others injured.You use AI every day. articles.title: Ship attacks in Persian Gulf: Shipping minister Sonowal asks maritime regulator to be on high alert in high-risk areas
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Amid recent attacks on commercial vessels with Indian crew members in the Persian Gulf, shipping minister Sarbananda Sonowal on Thursday
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Amid recent attacks on commercial vessels with Indian crew members in the Persian Gulf, shipping minister Sarbananda Sonowal on Thursday directed the country’s maritime regulator to step up surveillance of high-risk areas, issue timely security advisories and sensitise seafarers about potential threats and precautionary measures.Between Nov 10 and 18, at least five reported incidents involving commercial vessels carrying Indian seafarers occurred in the Persian Gulf and around the Strait of Hormuz. The attacks involved projectiles and missiles, leaving Indian crew members injured, one missing and vessels damaged or evacuated.Chairing a review meeting on Thursday, Sonowal also directed the directorate general of maritime administration (DGMA) to maintain regular communication with shipping companies and vessel operators to ensure the safety of Indian seafarers. He asked officials to coordinate closely with the ministry of external affairs, Indian diplomatic missions, maritime stakeholders and international agencies to ensure prompt assistance in the event of an incident involving Indian vessels or seafarers.Currently, nine Indian-flagged or Indian-interest vessels carrying 161 Indian seafarers are in the Persian Gulf. In the Red Sea, eight Indian-flagged vessels have 210 Indian seafarers on board.The ministry is tracking more than 1,200 vessels and nearly 9,500 Indian seafarers in high-risk regions through a live dashboard launched for this purpose.So far, 104 incidents have been reported in the Persian Gulf, claiming 12 Indian lives.
